newsitem.title: UK: New UK regulatory body to have new powers - Liddell.
newsitem.headline: New UK regulatory body to have new powers - Liddell.

text.p: Britain's strengthened regulatory body for the financial services market will have new powers but it is not yet clear whether it will be able to enforce compensation, Treasury minister Helen Liddell said on Tuesday.
"It will indeed be equipped with new powers," she told BBC television in an interview.
"That is something the City and financial institutions will greatly welcome because there have been glaring problems over the last few years which people want to see rectified."

Earlier in the day finance minister Gordon Brown unveiled plans to overhaul the regulation of Britain's financial services industry, which has fallen victim to several embarrassing scandals over the last few years.
Brown said he wanted responsibility for supervising banks to be transferred from the Bank of England and given to a strengthened Securities and Investment Board (SIB).

Under the current regime a bank is supervised by the Bank of England but its stockbroking, asset management, retail financial services advisory arm and unit trusts operations are each supervised by a different agency.
Liddell said no final decisions had been taken on whether the new-style SIB would supervise building societies or would be able to force errant companies to pay out compensation.

"It (the SIB) will operate in a way that is not too dissimilar from its status at the moment in that it will be an organisation that operates within the private sector," she said, but gave no further details.
